    def uncolored_neighbors_mask(v, colored_mask):
        return bit_adj[v] & ~colored_mask

    # Helper: get colored neighbors mask
    def colored_neighbors_mask(v, colored_mask):
        return bit_adj[v] & colored_mask

    # Helper: get saturation (number of distinct colors in neighbors)
    def saturation(v, colored_mask, color_of):
        neighbor_mask = colored_neighbors_mask(v, colored_mask)
        if neighbor_mask == 0:
            return 0
        colors = set()
        u = neighbor_mask
        while u:
            # Extract lowest set bit
            lsb = u & -u
            i = (lsb.bit_length() - 1)
            colors.add(color_of[i])
            u ^= lsb
        return len(colors)

    # Helper: get degree in uncolored subgraph
    def uncolored_degree(v, uncolored_mask):
        return bit_count(uncolored_neighbors_mask(v, ~uncolored_mask & ((1 << n) - 1)))

    # Helper: greedy coloring with given order
    def greedy_color(order):
        color_of = [-1] * n
        for v in order:
            used = 0
            for u in neighbors[v]:
                if color_of[u] != -1:
                    used |= 1 << color_of[u]
            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            color_of[v] = c
        return color_of

    # Helper: validate coloring
    def is_valid(color_of):
        for u in range(n):
            for v in neighbors[u]:
                if u < v and color_of[u] == color_of[v]:
                    return False
        return True

    # Helper: normalize colors to 0..k-1
    def normalize(color_of):
        # Map colors to consecutive integers
        unique_colors = {}
        next_color = 0
        for i in range(n):
            c = color_of[i]
            if c not in unique_colors:
                unique_colors[c] = next_color
                next_color += 1
            color_of[i] = unique_colors[c]
        return color_of

    # Strategy 1: DSATUR with degree tie-breaking
    def dsatur():
        color_of = [-1] * n
        colored_mask = 0  # bitmask of colored vertices
        uncolored_mask = (1 << n) - 1

        for _ in range(n):
            # Select uncolored vertex with max saturation, tie-break by degree in uncolored subgraph
            best_v = -1
            best_sat = -1
            best_deg = -1
            for v in range(n):
                if not (colored_mask >> v) & 1:  # if v is uncolored
                    sat = saturation(v, colored_mask, color_of)
                    deg = uncolored_degree(v, uncolored_mask)
                    if sat > best_sat or (sat == best_sat and deg > best_deg):
                        best_sat = sat
                        best_deg = deg
                        best_v = v
            if best_v == -1:
                break  # should not happen
            # Assign smallest available color
            used = 0
            neighbor_mask = colored_neighbors_mask(best_v, colored_mask)
            u = neighbor_mask
            while u:
                lsb = u & -u
                i = (lsb.bit_length() - 1)
                used |= 1 << color_of[i]
                u ^= lsb
            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            color_of[best_v] = c
            colored_mask |= 1 << best_v
            uncolored_mask &= ~(1 << best_v)
        return normalize(color_of)

    # Strategy 2: RLF (Recursive Largest First)
    def rlf():
        color_of = [-1] * n
        uncolored_mask = (1 << n) - 1
        color = 0
        while uncolored_mask:
            # Build independent set for this color
            independent_set = 0  # bitmask
            # Start with vertex of max degree in uncolored subgraph
            best_v = -1
            best_deg = -1
            temp_mask = uncolored_mask
            while temp_mask:
                lsb = temp_mask & -temp_mask
                v = (lsb.bit_length() - 1)
                deg = uncolored_degree(v, uncolored_mask)
                if deg > best_deg:
                    best_deg = deg
                    best_v = v
                temp_mask ^= lsb
            if best_v == -1:
                break
            independent_set |= 1 << best_v
            # U: vertices not adjacent to any in independent_set (eligible)
            # W: vertices adjacent to at least one in independent_set (ineligible)
            # Initially, W = neighbors of best_v, U = uncolored \ {best_v} \ W
            forbidden_mask = bit_adj[best_v] & uncolored_mask
            eligible_mask = uncolored_mask & ~(1 << best_v) & ~forbidden_mask
            # While there are eligible vertices
            while eligible_mask:
                # Select u in eligible_mask with max |N(u) ∩ W|, tie-break by min degree in G[U]
                best_u = -1
                best_score = -1
                best_u_deg = -1
                temp = eligible_mask
                while temp:
                    lsb = temp & -temp
                    u = (lsb.bit_length() - 1)
                    # Score: number of neighbors in W (forbidden_mask)
                    w_neighbors = bit_adj[u] & forbidden_mask
                    score = bit_count(w_neighbors)
                    # Tie-breaker: degree in G[U] (eligible subgraph)
                    u_deg = uncolored_degree(u, eligible_mask)
                    if score > best_score or (score == best_score and u_deg < best_u_deg):
                        best_score = score
                        best_u_deg = u_deg
                        best_u = u
                    temp ^= lsb
                if best_u == -1:
                    break
                # Add best_u to independent set
                independent_set |= 1 << best_u
                # Update forbidden_mask and eligible_mask
                forbidden_mask |= bit_adj[best_u] & uncolored_mask
                eligible_mask &= ~(1 << best_u)
                eligible_mask &= ~forbidden_mask  # remove newly forbidden
            # Assign color to all in independent_set
            temp = independent_set
            while temp:
                lsb = temp & -temp
                v = (lsb.bit_length() - 1)
                color_of[v] = color
                temp ^= lsb
            # Remove independent_set from uncolored
            uncolored_mask &= ~independent_set
            color += 1
        return normalize(color_of)

    # Strategy 3: Smallest-Last (Matula & Beck) ordering + greedy
    def smallest_last():
        # Build degeneracy ordering (smallest last)
        degrees = [len(neighbors[i]) for i in range(n)]
        # We'll simulate peeling
        order = []
        remaining = set(range(n))
        # Current degrees in remaining graph
        curr_deg = degrees[:]
        # Bucket sort by degree
        max_deg = max(degrees) if n > 0 else 0
        buckets = [[] for _ in range(max_deg + 1)]
        for v in range(n):
            buckets[curr_deg[v]].append(v)
        # Pointer to current non-empty bucket
        ptr = 0
        for _ in range(n):
            # Find next non-empty bucket
            while ptr <= max_deg and not buckets[ptr]:
                ptr += 1
            if ptr > max_deg:
                break  # should not happen
            v = buckets[ptr].pop()
            order.append(v)
            remaining.remove(v)
            # Update neighbors
            for u in neighbors[v]:
                if u in remaining:
                    old_deg = curr_deg[u]
                    curr_deg[u] -= 1
                    if old_deg < len(buckets):
                        buckets[old_deg].remove(u)  # O(n) but n<=100
                    if curr_deg[u] < len(buckets):
                        buckets[curr_deg[u]].append(u)
                    # Update ptr if needed
                    if curr_deg[u] < ptr:
                        ptr = curr_deg[u]
        # Reverse to get coloring order (largest first in removal)
        order.reverse()
        return greedy_color(order)

    # Run all strategies and pick best (fewest colors)
    strategies = [dsatur, rlf, smallest_last]
    best_coloring = None
    best_num_colors = float('inf')

    for strat in strategies:
        try:
            coloring = strat()
            if not is_valid(coloring):
                continue
            num_colors = max(coloring) + 1 if n > 0 else 0
            if num_colors < best_num_colors:
                best_num_colors = num_colors
                best_coloring = coloring
        except Exception:
            continue

    # Fallback: if all failed, use simple greedy by degree
    if best_coloring is None:
        order = sorted(range(n), key=lambda x: len(neighbors[x]), reverse=True)
        best_coloring = greedy_color(order)
        best_coloring = normalize(best_coloring)

    # Kempe chain-based color reduction
    def kempe_reduce(color_of):
        # Try to eliminate the highest color class
        while True:
            # Find current number of colors
            colors_used = set(color_of)
            if not colors_used:
                break
            max_color = max(colors_used)
            # Try to eliminate color class max_color
            vertices_of_max_color = [v for v in range(n) if color_of[v] == max_color]
            if not vertices_of_max_color:
                # Already empty, compact and continue
                color_of = normalize(color_of)
                continue
            made_progress = False
            # For each vertex in the max color class
            for v in vertices_of_max_color:
                # Try to recolor v to a lower color without conflict
                neighbor_colors = set()
                for u in neighbors[v]:
                    if color_of[u] != -1:
                        neighbor_colors.add(color_of[u])
                for c in range(max_color):  # try colors 0..max_color-1
                    if c not in neighbor_colors:
                        # Direct recolor possible
                        color_of[v] = c
                        made_progress = True
                        break
                if made_progress:
                    break
                # Try Kempe chain swaps with each lower color
                for c in range(max_color):
                    # Consider (c, max_color) Kempe chain
                    # We'll check if v is in a component that does not contain any vertex of color c
                    # that is adjacent to a vertex of color max_color? Actually standard:
                    # We can swap if the Kempe chain starting at v of colors (c, max_color)
                    # does not reach any neighbor of v that has color c.
                    # Build the Kempe chain component containing v using only colors c and max_color
                    from collections import deque
                    visited = [False] * n
                    queue = deque([v])
                    visited[v] = True
                    component = set()
                    while queue:
                        node = queue.popleft()
                        component.add(node)
                        for u in neighbors[node]:
                            if not visited[u] and color_of[u] in (c, max_color):
                                visited[u] = True
                                queue.append(u)
                    # Check if any neighbor of v has color c and is in the component?
                    # Actually, we can swap if no neighbor of v with color c is in the component.
                    conflict = False
                    for u in neighbors[v]:
                        if color_of[u] == c and u in component:
                            conflict = True
                            break
                    if not conflict:
                        # Swap colors c and max_color in the component
                        for node in component:
                            if color_of[node] == c:
                                color_of[node] = max_color
                            elif color_of[node] == max_color:
                                color_of[node] = c
                        made_progress = True
                        break
                if made_progress:
                    break
            if not made_progress:
                break
            # Compact colors
            color_of = normalize(color_of)
        return color_of

    # Apply Kempe reduction
    try:
        best_coloring = kempe_reduce(best_coloring)
        best_coloring = normalize(best_coloring)
    except Exception:
        pass

    # Final validation and normalization
    if not is_valid(best_coloring):
        # Last resort: greedy by degree
        order = sorted(range(n), key=lambda x: len(neighbors[x]), reverse=True)
        best_coloring = greedy_color(order)
        best_coloring = normalize(best_coloring)

    return best_coloring

import math
import random

def color_graph(adj: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
    if not adj:
        return []
    n = len(adj)
    if n == 0:
        return []
    if n == 1:
        return [0]

    # Convert to adjacency list if needed
    if len(adj) > 0 and len(adj[0]) == n and all(isinstance(x, int) and x in (0, 1) for row in adj for x in row):
        graph = [[] for _ in range(n)]
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(n):
                if adj[i][j] == 1 and i != j:
                    graph[i].append(j)
    else:
        graph = [list(neigh) for neigh in adj]

    # Tarjan's algorithm for biconnected components (vertex-biconnected, blocks)
    disc = [-1] * n
    low = [-1] * n
    parent = [-1] * n
    st = []
    time = 0
    blocks = []  # list of list of vertices (each block)
    cut = [False] * n  # cut vertices

    def dfs(u):
        nonlocal time
        disc[u] = low[u] = time
        time += 1
        children = 0
        for v in graph[u]:
            if disc[v] == -1:
                parent[v] = u
                children += 1
                st.append((u, v))
                dfs(v)
                low[u] = min(low[u], low[v])
                if (parent[u] == -1 and children > 1) or (parent[u] != -1 and low[v] >= disc[u]):
                    cut[u] = True
                    block = []
                    while True:
                        e = st.pop()
                        block.append(e[0])
                        block.append(e[1])
                        if e == (u, v):
                            break
                    blocks.append(list(set(block)))
            elif v != parent[u] and disc[v] < disc[u]:
                low[u] = min(low[u], disc[v])
                st.append((u, v))
        # For root, no special handling needed beyond children count

    for i in range(n):
        if disc[i] == -1:
            dfs(i)
            if st:
                block = []
                while st:
                    e = st.pop()
                    block.append(e[0])
                    block.append(e[1])
                blocks.append(list(set(block)))

    # If no blocks found (should not happen for n>=1), fallback to whole graph
    if not blocks:
        blocks = [list(range(n))]

    # Build block-cut tree: bipartite graph between blocks and cut vertices
    # We will assign an id to each cut vertex and each block
    cut_vertices = [i for i in range(n) if cut[i]]
    cut_id_map = {v: idx for idx, v in enumerate(cut_vertices)}
    num_cuts = len(cut_vertices)
    num_blocks = len(blocks)
    # For each block, which cut vertices it contains
    block_cuts = []
    for b in blocks:
        bc = [v for v in b if cut[v]]
        block_cuts.append(bc)

    # For each cut vertex, which blocks it belongs to
    cut_blocks = [[] for _ in range(num_cuts)]
    for bid, bc in enumerate(block_cuts):
        for v in bc:
            cid = cut_id_map[v]
            cut_blocks[cid].append(bid)

    # Build tree: nodes 0..num_blocks-1 are blocks, num_blocks..num_blocks+num_cuts-1 are cut vertices
    tree_adj = [[] for _ in range(num_blocks + num_cuts)]
    for bid in range(num_blocks):
        for v in block_cuts[bid]:
            cid = cut_id_map[v]
            tree_adj[bid].append(num_blocks + cid)
            tree_adj[num_blocks + cid].append(bid)

    # We will color the block-cut tree via BFS, starting from an arbitrary block
    # Each block will be colored internally, and we will enforce consistency at cut vertices
    # We maintain for each cut vertex a fixed color that all incident blocks must use for that vertex
    cut_vertex_color = [-1] * num_cuts  # color assigned to each cut vertex
    block_coloring = [None] * num_blocks  # each will be a dict: vertex -> color in global coloring

    # Helper: color a block (induced subgraph) with possible pre-colored cut vertices
    def color_block(block_vertices, precolored):
        # block_vertices: list of global vertex indices
        # precolored: dict {v: color} for some v in block_vertices that are cut vertices with fixed color
        # Returns: dict {v: color} for all v in block_vertices, respecting precolored and minimizing colors
        # If conflict, returns None
        # Build subgraph adjacency
        local_index = {v: i for i, v in enumerate(block_vertices)}
        m = len(block_vertices)
        local_adj = [[] for _ in range(m)]
        for v in block_vertices:
            i = local_index[v]
            for w in graph[v]:
                if w in local_index:
                    j = local_index[w]
                    local_adj[i].append(j)
        # Convert to adjacency matrix for bitmask? Since m <= n <= 100, we can use simple DSATUR
        # We'll implement DSATUR with bitmask for speed
        # Precompute neighbor bitmask
        bit_adj = [0] * m
        for i in range(m):
            for j in local_adj[i]:
                bit_adj[i] |= (1 << j)
        # DSATUR
        colored = [False] * m
        color = [-1] * m
        # saturation: number of distinct colors in neighbors
        saturation = [0] * m
        # neighbor colorsets as bitmask
        neighbor_colors = [0] * m
        # Initialize with precolored
        for v, c in precolored.items():
            i = local_index[v]
            color[i] = c
            colored[i] = True
            # update neighbors
            nb = bit_adj[i]
            while nb:
                j = (nb & -nb).bit_length() - 1
                nb &= nb - 1
                if not colored[j]:
                    neighbor_colors[j] |= (1 << c)
                    saturation[j] = neighbor_colors[j].bit_count()
        # Main loop
        for _ in range(m):
            # select uncolored vertex with max saturation, tie-break by degree in uncolored subgraph, then index
            max_sat = -1
            candidates = []
            for i in range(m):
                if not colored[i]:
                    sat = saturation[i]
                    if sat > max_sat:
                        max_sat = sat
                        candidates = [i]
                    elif sat == max_sat:
                        candidates.append(i)
            if max_sat == -1:
                break  # should not happen
            # tie-break: degree in uncolored subgraph
            max_deg = -1
            selected = -1
            for i in candidates:
                # count uncolored neighbors
                deg = 0
                nb = bit_adj[i]
                while nb:
                    j = (nb & -nb).bit_length() - 1
                    nb &= nb - 1
                    if not colored[j]:
                        deg += 1
                if deg > max_deg:
                    max_deg = deg
                    selected = i
                elif deg == max_deg and i < selected:
                    selected = i
            v = selected
            # find smallest color not in neighbor_colors[v]
            c = 0
            while neighbor_colors[v] & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            color[v] = c
            colored[v] = True
            # update neighbors
            nb = bit_adj[v]
            while nb:
                j = (nb & -nb).bit_length() - 1
                nb &= nb - 1
                if not colored[j]:
                    neighbor_colors[j] |= (1 << c)
                    saturation[j] = neighbor_colors[j].bit_count()
        # Build result dict
        res = {}
        for i in range(m):
            if colored[i]:
                res[block_vertices[i]] = color[i]
            else:
                # This should not happen if block is connected? but just in case
                return None
        return res

    # BFS over block-cut tree
    from collections import deque
    visited = [False] * (num_blocks + num_cuts)
    # Start with block 0 if exists, else any
    start = 0
    q = deque([start])
    visited[start] = True
    while q:
        u = q.popleft()
        if u < num_blocks:  # block node
            bid = u
            block = blocks[bid]
            # collect precolored cut vertices in this block
            precolored = {}
            for v in block:
                if cut[v]:
                    cid = cut_id_map[v]
                    if cut_vertex_color[cid] != -1:
                        precolored[v] = cut_vertex_color[cid]
            # color the block
            coloring = color_block(block, precolored)
            if coloring is None:
                # fallback: ignore precolored and color freely, then we will have conflict later? 
                # For now, try without precolored
                coloring = color_block(block, {})
                if coloring is None:
                    # last resort: greedy
                    # simple greedy ordering by degree
                    indices = list(range(len(block)))
                    indices.sort(key=lambda x: -len([w for w in graph[block[x]] if w in block]))
                    color_local = [-1] * len(block)
                    for idx in indices:
                        v = block[idx]
                        used = set()
                        for w in graph[v]:
                            if w in block:
                                ci = color_local[block.index(w)]
                                if ci != -1:
                                    used.add(ci)
                        c = 0
                        while c in used:
                            c += 1
                        color_local[idx] = c
                    coloring = {block[i]: color_local[i] for i in range(len(block))}
            block_coloring[bid] = coloring
            # Now, for each cut vertex in this block, if not yet assigned, assign its color from this block's coloring
            for v in block:
                if cut[v]:
                    cid = cut_id_map[v]
                    if cut_vertex_color[cid] == -1:
                        cut_vertex_color[cid] = coloring[v]
        else:  # cut vertex node
            cid = u - num_blocks
            # For each adjacent block, if not visited, add to queue
            for nb in tree_adj[u]:
                if not visited[nb]:
                    visited[nb] = True
                    q.append(nb)

    # After BFS, we should have colored all blocks and assigned colors to all cut vertices
    # Build final coloring
    final_color = [0] * n
    for bid in range(num_blocks):
        coloring = block_coloring[bid]
        if coloring is None:
            # fallback: should not happen
            continue
        for v, c in coloring.items():
            final_color[v] = c
    # Ensure cut vertices have consistent color (should be by construction)
    for v in range(n):
        if cut[v]:
            cid = cut_id_map[v]
            if cut_vertex_color[cid] != -1:
                final_color[v] = cut_vertex_color[cid]

    # Compact colors: remap to 0..k-1
    unique_colors = set(final_color)
    if not unique_colors:
        return [0] * n
    mapping = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(sorted(unique_colors))]
    final_color = [mapping[c] for c in final_color]

    return final_color

                U.remove(u)

                W.update(nbrs_u)
                U -= nbrs_u

            for v in S:
                coloring[v] = color
            uncolored -= S
            color += 1

    # Smallest-Last ( degeneracy ordering )
    def smallest_last():
        # Compute degeneracy ordering by repeatedly removing min degree vertex
        remaining = set(range(n))
        degree = [len(neighbors[i]) for i in range(n)]
        order = []
        # Current degrees in the remaining subgraph
        curr_degree = degree[:]
        # Bucket queue for efficiency
        max_deg = max(degree) if n > 0 else 0
        buckets = [[] for _ in range(max_deg + 1)]
        for v in range(n):
            d = curr_degree[v]
            if d < len(buckets):
                buckets[d].append(v)
            else:
                # extend buckets if needed (should not happen)
                buckets.extend([[] for _ in range(d - len(buckets) + 1)])
                buckets[d].append(v)
        # Pointer to current min non-empty bucket
        min_ptr = 0
        while remaining:
            # Find next non-empty bucket
            while min_ptr < len(buckets) and not buckets[min_ptr]:
                min_ptr += 1
            if min_ptr >= len(buckets):
                break  # should not happen
            # Get a vertex from bucket[min_ptr]
            while buckets[min_ptr] and buckets[min_ptr][-1] not in remaining:
                buckets[min_ptr].pop()
            if not buckets[min_ptr]:
                min_ptr += 1
                continue
            v = buckets[min_ptr].pop()
            if v not in remaining:
                continue
            order.append(v)
            remaining.remove(v)
            # Update neighbors
            for u in neighbors[v]:
                if u in remaining:
                    d = curr_degree[u]
                    # remove u from bucket[d]
                    if u in buckets[d]:
                        buckets[d].remove(u)  # O(bucket size), but small
                    curr_degree[u] -= 1
                    d_new = curr_degree[u]
                    if d_new < len(buckets):
                        buckets[d_new].append(u)
                    else:
                        buckets.extend([[] for _ in range(d_new - len(buckets) + 1)])
                        buckets[d_new].append(u)
                    if d_new < min_ptr:
                        min_ptr = d_new
        # Color in reverse order
        coloring = [-1] * n
        for v in reversed(order):
            used = set()
            for u in neighbors[v]:
                if coloring[u] != -1:
                    used.add(coloring[u])
            c = 0
            while c in used:
                c += 1
            coloring[v] = c
        return coloring

    candidates = []
    start = time.time()
    # DSATUR
    c1 = dsatur()
    if time.time() - start < 0.05:  # 50 ms budget
        candidates.append(c1)
    # RLF
    c2 = rlf()
    if time.time() - start < 0.05:
        candidates.append(c2)
    # Smallest-Last
    c3 = smallest_last()
    if time.time() - start < 0.05:
        candidates.append(c3)

    # Select best candidate (fewest colors)
    best_coloring = None
    best_k = float('inf')
    for col in candidates:
        if not is_valid(col):
            continue
        col_norm = normalize(col[:])  # work on copy
        k = max(col_norm) + 1 if n > 0 else 0
        if k < best_k:
            best_k = k
            best_coloring = col_norm

    if best_coloring is None:
        order = sorted(range(n), key=lambda x: len(neighbors[x]), reverse=True)

        for v in order:
            used = set()
            for u in neighbors[v]:
                if coloring[u] != -1:
                    used.add(coloring[u])
            c = 0
            while c in used:
                c += 1
            coloring[v] = c

    # Kempe chain color reduction
    def kempe_reduce(coloring):
        # Make a copy to work on
        col = coloring[:]
        changed = True
        while changed and time.time() - start < 0.05:
            changed = False
            # Find color classes
            classes = {}
            for v in range(n):
                c = col[v]
                if c not in classes:
                    classes[c] = []
                classes[c].append(v)
            # Sort colors by class size ascending
            sorted_colors = sorted(classes.keys(), key=lambda c: len(classes[c]))
            # Try to eliminate smallest color class
            for c in sorted_colors:
                if time.time() - start >= 0.05:
                    break
                if c not in classes or len(classes[c]) == 0:
                    continue
                # Try to recolor each vertex in class c
                eliminated = True
                for v in classes[c][:]:  # iterate over copy
                    if time.time() - start >= 0.05:
                        break

                    neighbor_colors = set()
                    for u in neighbors[v]:
                        if col[u] != -1:
                            neighbor_colors.add(col[u])
                    for c_new in range(c):  # only try lower colors
                        if c_new not in neighbor_colors:
                            col[v] = c_new
                            changed = True
                            break
                    if col[v] == c:  # not reassigned directly
                        # Try Kempe chains with each lower color
                        for c_new in range(c):
                            if time.time() - start >= 0.05:
                                break
                            # Build (c, c_new) Kempe chain containing v
                            # We'll try to swap if it frees color c for v
                            # BFS to get component
                            from collections import deque
                            visited = set()
                            queue = deque([v])
                            visited.add(v)
                            component = set()
                            while queue:
                                node = queue.popleft()
                                component.add(node)
                                for u in neighbors[node]:
                                    if col[u] == c or col[u] == c_new:
                                        if u not in visited:
                                            visited.add(u)
                                            queue.append(u)

                            # After swap, v would have color c_new
                            # Check if any neighbor of v has color c_new (outside component)
                            conflict = False
                            for u in neighbors[v]:
                                if u not in component and col[u] == c_new:
                                    conflict = True
                                    break
                            if not conflict:
                                # Perform swap: c <-> c_new in component
                                for node in component:
                                    if col[node] == c:
                                        col[node] = c_new
                                    elif col[node] == c_new:
                                        col[node] = c
                                changed = True
                                # After swap, v is now color c_new, so removed from class c
                                break
                    if col[v] != c:
                        # Successfully recolored v
                        pass
                    else:
                        # Could not recolor v
                        eliminated = False
                if eliminated and len(classes.get(c, [])) == 0:
                    # Color c eliminated, break to restart
                    break
            # Normalize colors to be consecutive
            col = normalize(col)
        return col

    # Apply Kempe reduction if time permits
    if time.time() - start < 0.05:
        best_coloring = kempe_reduce(best_coloring)
        best_coloring = normalize(best_coloring)

    # Final validation and normalization
    if not is_valid(best_coloring):
        # Last resort: greedy
        order = sorted(range(n), key=lambda x: len(neighbors[x]), reverse=True)
        coloring = [-1] * n
        for v in order:
            used = set()
            for u in neighbors[v]:
                if coloring[u] != -1:
                    used.add(coloring[u])
            c = 0
            while c in used:
                c += 1
            coloring[v] = c
        best_coloring = normalize(coloring)

    return best_coloring

    def greedy_color(order):

            for u in neighbors[v]:

                    used.add(color[u])
            c = 0
            while c in used:
                c += 1
            color[v] = c

    def dsatur():

            # assign smallest available color

            # update saturation of uncolored neighbors
            for u in neighbors[v]:

    def rlf():

            deg_sub = {v: len(neighbors[v] & uncolored) for v in uncolored}
            # start with vertex of max degree
            v = max(uncolored, key=lambda x: (deg_sub[x], random.random()))
            independent_set = {v}

            U = uncolored - {v} - neighbors[v]

            while U:
                # select u in U with max neighbors in W, tie-break by min degree in U
                def score(u):
                    w_count = len(neighbors[u] & W)
                    u_deg = len(neighbors[u] & U)
                    return (w_count, -u_deg, random.random())
                u = max(U, key=score)
                independent_set.add(u)
                U.remove(u)
                # move neighbors of u from U to W
                nbrs_u = neighbors[u] & U
                U -= nbrs_u
                W |= nbrs_u

            for v in independent_set:

                uncolored.remove(v)

                    old_deg = deg[u]
                    buckets[old_deg].remove(u)
                    deg[u] -= 1
                    new_deg = deg[u]

def color_graph(adj: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:

                    break

    neighbors = [[] for _ in range(n)]

            for j in range(n):
                if adj[i][j] == 1:
                    bit_adj[i] |= (1 << j)
                    neighbors[i].append(j)

        for i in range(n):
            for j in adj[i]:
                bit_adj[i] |= (1 << j)
                neighbors[i].append(j)

    def bit_count(x: int) -> int:
        return x.bit_count()

    def dsatur() -> list[int]:
        color = [-1] * n
        # Saturation: for each vertex, bitmask of colors used by colored neighbors
        sat = [0] * n

        deg_uncolored = [bit_count(bit_adj[i]) for i in range(n)]

            max_sat = -1
            max_deg = -1
            for u in uncolored:

                d = deg_uncolored[u]

                    max_deg = d
                    v = u

            U = set()
            W = set()

                if bit_adj[u] & sum((1 << w) for w in S):

                else:
                    U.add(u)

            if changed:

        # Map used colors to consecutive integers

        mapping = {old: new for new, old in enumerate(used_colors)}
        color = [mapping[c] for c in color]

        sat = [0] * n

        neighbor_colors = [0] * n

                    max_sat = sat[u]
                    max_deg = degrees[u]
                    v = u

            for u in adj[v]:

    def rlf():

            # Build independent set for this color

                cnt = 0
                for v in adj[u]:

                best_score = -1

                U.remove(u)

                        W.add(w)

def color_graph(adj: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:

    if len(adj) > 0 and len(adj[0]) == len(adj):

        for row in adj:
            for val in row:

                    break

        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(n):

                    bit_adj[i] |= (1 << j)

        adj_list = [list(neighbors) for neighbors in adj]
        bit_adj = [0] * n
        for i in range(n):
            for j in adj_list[i]:
                bit_adj[i] |= (1 << j)

    best_coloring = None
    best_k = float('inf')

    # Helper: greedy coloring given an order
    def greedy_coloring(order):
        colors = [-1] * n
        for v in order:
            used = 0
            for u in adj_list[v]:
                if colors[u] != -1:
                    used |= (1 << colors[u])
            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            colors[v] = c
        return colors

    # Heuristic 1: DSATUR with bitmask optimization
    def dsatur():
        colors = [-1] * n
        # saturation mask: bitmask of colors used by neighbors
        sat_mask = [0] * n
        # degree in uncolored subgraph
        uncolored_deg = [len(adj_list[i]) for i in range(n)]
        uncolored = set(range(n))
        for _ in range(n):
            # select vertex with max saturation, tie-break by degree then index
            v = -1
            max_sat = -1
            max_deg = -1
            for u in uncolored:
                sat_count = sat_mask[u].bit_count()
                if sat_count > max_sat or (sat_count == max_sat and uncolored_deg[u] > max_deg) or \
                   (sat_count == max_sat and uncolored_deg[u] == max_deg and u > v):
                    max_sat = sat_count
                    max_deg = uncolored_deg[u]
                    v = u
            # assign smallest available color
            used = sat_mask[v]
            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            colors[v] = c
            uncolored.remove(v)
            # update neighbors
            for u in adj_list[v]:
                if u in uncolored:
                    sat_mask[u] |= (1 << c)
                    uncolored_deg[u] -= 1
        return colors

    # Heuristic 2: RLF (Recursive Largest First)
    def rlf():
        colors = [-1] * n
        uncolored = set(range(n))
        color = 0
        while uncolored:
            # build maximal independent set for this color
            S = set()
            # choose vertex with max degree in G[uncolored]
            v = max(uncolored, key=lambda x: sum(1 for y in adj_list[x] if y in uncolored))
            S.add(v)
            # U: vertices not adjacent to S, W: vertices adjacent to S
            U = {u for u in uncolored if u not in S and not any(w in S for w in adj_list[u])}
            W = {u for u in uncolored if u not in S and u not in U}
            while U:
                # select u in U with max |N(u) ∩ W|
                u_star = -1
                max_nw = -1
                min_deg_U = float('inf')
                for u in U:
                    nw = sum(1 for w in adj_list[u] if w in W)
                    if nw > max_nw or (nw == max_nw and sum(1 for y in adj_list[u] if y in U) < min_deg_U) or \
                       (nw == max_nw and sum(1 for y in adj_list[u] if y in U) == min_deg_U and u > u_star):
                        max_nw = nw
                        min_deg_U = sum(1 for y in adj_list[u] if y in U)
                        u_star = u
                S.add(u_star)
                U.remove(u_star)
                # move neighbors of u_star in U to W
                for w in adj_list[u_star]:
                    if w in U:
                        U.remove(w)
                        W.add(w)
            # assign color to all in S
            for v in S:
                colors[v] = color
            uncolored -= S
            color += 1
        return colors

    # Heuristic 3: Smallest-Last ordering
    def smallest_last():
        # core decomposition to get order
        deg = [len(adj_list[i]) for i in range(n)]
        # buckets for degree

        buckets = [[] for _ in range(max_deg + 1)]
        pos = [0] * n
        for i in range(n):
            d = deg[i]
            buckets[d].append(i)
            pos[i] = len(buckets[d]) - 1
        # current min degree
        min_deg = 0
        order = []
        # copy of degrees
        curr_deg = deg[:]
        # for tracking position in bucket
        bucket_pos = [0] * n
        for i in range(n):
            buckets[i] = []
        for i in range(n):
            d = curr_deg[i]
            if d < len(buckets):
                buckets[d].append(i)
                bucket_pos[i] = len(buckets[d]) - 1

        for _ in range(n):

                    buckets[d].pop(bucket_pos[u])
                    if bucket_pos[u] < len(buckets[d]):

                        last = buckets[d][-1]
                        buckets[d][bucket_pos[u]] = last
                        bucket_pos[last] = bucket_pos[u]
                    curr_deg[u] -= 1
                    d2 = curr_deg[u]
                    if d2 < len(buckets):
                        buckets[d2].append(u)
                        bucket_pos[u] = len(buckets[d2]) - 1
                    else:
                        # extend buckets if needed (should not happen as degree decreases)
                        while len(buckets) <= d2:
                            buckets.append([])
                        buckets[d2].append(u)
                        bucket_pos[u] = len(buckets[d2]) - 1
            # after removal, adjust min_deg if needed
            if min_deg > 0 and not buckets[min_deg-1]:
                min_deg -= 1
        # color in reverse order
        colors = [-1] * n
        for v in reversed(order):
            used = 0
            for u in adj_list[v]:
                if colors[u] != -1:
                    used |= (1 << colors[u])
            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            colors[v] = c
        return colors

    # Generate candidate colorings
    candidates = []
    try:
        c1 = dsatur()
        candidates.append(c1)
    except:
        pass
    try:
        c2 = rlf()
        candidates.append(c2)
    except:
        pass
    try:
        c3 = smallest_last()
        candidates.append(c3)
    except:
        pass

    # Also try Welsh-Powell (degree ordering)
    order_wp = sorted(range(n), key=lambda x: len(adj_list[x]), reverse=True)
    c_wp = greedy_coloring(order_wp)
    candidates.append(c_wp)

    # Evaluate candidates
    for coloring in candidates:
        # validate
        valid = True
        for u in range(n):
            for v in adj_list[u]:
                if u < v and coloring[u] == coloring[v]:
                    valid = False
                    break
            if not valid:
                break
        if not valid:
            continue
        # compact colors
        unique = set(coloring)
        mapping = {}
        for i, col in enumerate(sorted(unique)):
            mapping[col] = i

        unique = set(best_coloring)
        mapping = {col: i for i, col in enumerate(sorted(unique))}
        best_coloring = [mapping[best_coloring[i]] for i in range(n)]
        best_k = len(unique)

    # Kempe chain color reduction
    def kempe_reduction(coloring):
        # make a copy
        col = coloring[:]
        changed = True
        while changed:
            changed = False
            # find color classes
            classes = {}
            for v in range(n):
                c = col[v]
                if c not in classes:
                    classes[c] = []
                classes[c].append(v)
            # sort colors by class size
            sorted_colors = sorted(classes.keys(), key=lambda c: len(classes[c]))
            # try to eliminate smallest color classes
            for c in sorted_colors:
                if c >= len(classes) - 1:  # not the smallest? break when we try all but largest
                    break
                S = classes[c]
                # try to recolor each vertex in S
                eliminated = True
                for v in S:
                    # try direct reassignment to a lower color
                    neighbor_colors = set()
                    for u in adj_list[v]:
                        neighbor_colors.add(col[u])
                    found = False
                    for target in range(c):  # only try colors < c
                        if target not in neighbor_colors:
                            col[v] = target
                            found = True
                            break
                    if found:
                        changed = True
                        continue
                    # try Kempe chains with each lower color
                    kempe_found = False
                    for target in range(c):
                        # BFS to find Kempe chain component of v for colors (c, target)
                        from collections import deque
                        visited = [False] * n
                        queue = deque([v])
                        visited[v] = True
                        component = []
                        while queue:
                            x = queue.popleft()
                            component.append(x)
                            for y in adj_list[x]:
                                if not visited[y] and (col[y] == c or col[y] == target):
                                    visited[y] = True
                                    queue.append(y)
                        # check if any neighbor of v in component has color target? 
                        # Actually, we want to see if we can swap: after swap, v becomes target
                        # and we need to ensure no neighbor of v becomes c (which would conflict if neighbor was target)
                        # Instead, standard: if the component does not contain any neighbor of v that is colored target,
                        # then swapping is safe for v.
                        safe = True
                        for u in adj_list[v]:
                            if col[u] == target and u in component:
                                safe = False
                                break
                        if safe:
                            # perform swap
                            for x in component:
                                if col[x] == c:
                                    col[x] = target
                                else:
                                    col[x] = c
                            changed = True
                            kempe_found = True
                            break
                    if kempe_found:
                        break
                    else:
                        eliminated = False
                        break
                if eliminated:
                    # remove color c: remap higher colors down
                    for v in range(n):
                        if col[v] > c:
                            col[v] -= 1
                    break  # restart while loop
        return col

    # Apply Kempe reduction
    try:
        reduced = kempe_reduction(best_coloring)
        # validate reduced
        valid = True
        for u in range(n):
            for v in adj_list[u]:
                if u < v and reduced[u] == reduced[v]:
                    valid = False
                    break
            if not valid:
                break
        if valid:
            # compact again
            unique = set(reduced)
            mapping = {col: i for i, col in enumerate(sorted(unique))]
            reduced = [mapping[reduced[i]] for i in range(n)]
            if len(unique) < best_k:
                best_coloring = reduced
    except:
        pass

    return best_coloring

    def greedy_clique(P):
        # P: bitmask of candidate vertices

            # Add u to clique

            # Update P: keep only neighbors of u in P

    uncolored = (1 << n) - 1

        for row in adj:
            if len(row) != n:
                is_matrix = False
                break
            for val in row:
                if val not in (0, 1):
                    is_matrix = False
                    break
            if not is_matrix:

                if adj[u][v] == 1:
                    neighbors[u].add(v)
                    bit_adj[u] |= (1 << v)
    else:
        for u in range(n):
            for v in adj[u]:
                neighbors[u].add(v)
                bit_adj[u] |= (1 << v)

    def is_valid(coloring):
        for u in range(n):
            cu = coloring[u]
            for v in neighbors[u]:
                if cu == coloring[v]:
                    return False
        return True

    def num_colors(coloring):
        return max(coloring) + 1 if coloring else 0

    def dsatur():
        coloring = [-1] * n
        # saturation: number of distinct colors in neighbors
        saturation = [0] * n
        # neighbor color masks for fast saturation update
        neighbor_color_mask = [0] * n
        uncolored = set(range(n))

        for _ in range(n):
            # select vertex with max saturation, tie-break by degree in uncolored subgraph
            v = -1
            max_sat = -1
            max_deg = -1
            for u in uncolored:
                sat_u = saturation[u]
                deg_u = len([w for w in neighbors[u] if w in uncolored])
                if sat_u > max_sat or (sat_u == max_sat and deg_u > max_deg) or (sat_u == max_sat and deg_u == max_deg and u > v):
                    max_sat = sat_u
                    max_deg = deg_u
                    v = u
            # assign smallest available color
            used = neighbor_color_mask[v]
            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            coloring[v] = c
            uncolored.remove(v)
            # update saturation and neighbor color masks for uncolored neighbors
            for w in neighbors[v]:
                if w in uncolored:
                    # if this color is new in w's neighborhood
                    if not (neighbor_color_mask[w] & (1 << c)):
                        neighbor_color_mask[w] |= (1 << c)
                        saturation[w] += 1
        return coloring

    # Helper: apply RLF heuristic
    def rlf():
        coloring = [-1] * n
        uncolored = set(range(n))
        color = 0
        while uncolored:
            # build maximal independent set for this color
            # start with vertex of max degree in uncolored subgraph
            v = -1
            max_deg = -1
            for u in uncolored:
                deg_u = len([w for w in neighbors[u] if w in uncolored])
                if deg_u > max_deg:
                    max_deg = deg_u
                    v = u
            independent_set = {v}
            # U: vertices not adjacent to any in independent_set (eligible)
            # W: vertices adjacent to at least one in independent_set (ineligible)
            U = uncolored - {v} - neighbors[v]
            W = (uncolored - {v}) & neighbors[v]
            while U:
                # select u in U with max neighbors in W
                u = -1
                max_w_neighbors = -1
                min_deg_U = float('inf')
                for cand in U:
                    w_neighbors = len([w for w in neighbors[cand] if w in W])
                    deg_U = len([w for w in neighbors[cand] if w in U])
                    if w_neighbors > max_w_neighbors or (w_neighbors == max_w_neighbors and deg_U < min_deg_U) or (w_neighbors == max_w_neighbors and deg_U == min_deg_U and cand < u):
                        max_w_neighbors = w_neighbors
                        min_deg_U = deg_U
                        u = cand
                independent_set.add(u)
                U.remove(u)
                # move neighbors of u that are in U to W
                nbrs_in_U = neighbors[u] & U
                W |= nbrs_in_U
                U -= nbrs_in_U
            # assign color to all in independent_set
            for vertex in independent_set:
                coloring[vertex] = color
                uncolored.remove(vertex)
            color += 1
        return coloring

    # Helper: apply smallest-last ordering (degeneracy ordering)
    def smallest_last():
        # core decomposition to get removal order
        degrees = [len(neighbors[i]) for i in range(n)]
        # bins for vertices by degree
        max_deg = max(degrees) if n > 0 else 0
        bins = [[] for _ in range(max_deg + 1)]
        pos = [0] * n
        for i in range(n):
            d = degrees[i]
            bins[d].append(i)
            pos[i] = len(bins[d]) - 1
        # current degree and bin pointers
        curr_deg = degrees[:]
        # order of removal (smallest last)
        order = []
        for _ in range(n):
            # find non-empty bin with smallest index
            d = 0
            while d <= max_deg and not bins[d]:
                d += 1
            if d > max_deg:
                break
            v = bins[d].pop()
            order.append(v)
            # update neighbors
            for w in neighbors[v]:
                if curr_deg[w] > d:  # w not yet removed
                    # remove w from its current bin
                    dw = curr_deg[w]
                    bins[dw].pop(pos[w])
                    if bins[dw]:
                        # update position of last element moved to fill gap
                        last_v = bins[dw][-1]
                        pos[last_v] = pos[w]
                    curr_deg[w] -= 1
                    # add w to bin for new degree
                    new_dw = curr_deg[w]
                    bins[new_dw].append(w)
                    pos[w] = len(bins[new_dw]) - 1
        # color in reverse order
        coloring = [-1] * n
        for v in reversed(order):
            used = 0
            for w in neighbors[v]:
                if coloring[w] != -1:
                    used |= (1 << coloring[w])
            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            coloring[v] = c
        return coloring

    # Helper: Kempe chain swap for colors a and b, starting from vertex v
    def kempe_swap(coloring, a, b, v):
        # returns new coloring with colors a and b swapped in the Kempe chain of v containing color a
        # or None if v is not color a
        if coloring[v] != a:
            return None
        # BFS to get the (a,b)-Kempe chain component containing v
        stack = [v]
        visited = set([v])
        while stack:
            u = stack.pop()
            for w in neighbors[u]:
                if w not in visited and coloring[w] in (a, b):
                    visited.add(w)
                    stack.append(w)
        # swap colors a<->b in the component
        new_coloring = coloring[:]
        for u in visited:
            if new_coloring[u] == a:
                new_coloring[u] = b
            else:
                new_coloring[u] = a
        return new_coloring

    # Helper: try to eliminate the last color using Kempe chains and direct reassignment
    def reduce_colors(coloring):
        k = num_colors(coloring)
        if k <= 1:
            return coloring
        # try to eliminate color k-1
        target_color = k - 1
        vertices_target = [v for v in range(n) if coloring[v] == target_color]
        # try direct reassignment first
        for v in vertices_target:
            used = 0
            for w in neighbors[v]:
                if coloring[w] != target_color:  # ignore same color (shouldn't be adjacent anyway)
                    used |= (1 << coloring[w])
            # find smallest color not used by neighbors
            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            if c < target_color:
                # reassign v to color c
                coloring[v] = c
        # recompute vertices still in target color
        vertices_target = [v for v in range(n) if coloring[v] == target_color]
        if not vertices_target:
            # target color eliminated, compact colors
            # map colors > target_color down by 1
            for v in range(n):
                if coloring[v] > target_color:
                    coloring[v] -= 1
            return coloring
        # try Kempe chains for each vertex in target color
        for v in vertices_target:
            for c in range(target_color):
                # check if v can be recolored to c via Kempe swap
                # only if there is no neighbor of v with color c (otherwise swap might not help directly)
                has_neighbor_c = any(coloring[w] == c for w in neighbors[v])
                if not has_neighbor_c:
                    # try Kempe chain swap between target_color and c
                    new_col = kempe_swap(coloring, target_color, c, v)
                    if new_col is not None and is_valid(new_col):
                        # accept the swap
                        coloring[:] = new_col
                        # after swap, v should now be color c
                        break
            else:
                continue
            break
        else:
            # no Kempe swap found for any vertex, cannot reduce
            return coloring
        # after successful swap, try to reduce again recursively
        return reduce_colors(coloring)

    # Generate candidate colorings

    # RLF
    col_rlf = rlf()
    if is_valid(col_rlf):
        candidates.append(col_rlf)
    # Smallest-Last
    col_sl = smallest_last()
    if is_valid(col_sl):
        candidates.append(col_sl)
    # If no valid candidate (should not happen), fallback to greedy
    if not candidates:
        # greedy ordering by degree descending
        order = sorted(range(n), key=lambda x: len(neighbors[x]), reverse=True)

                if coloring[w] != -1:

            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):

    best = min(candidates, key=num_colors)

    if not is_valid(best):

    unique_colors = {}

    for i in range(n):
        c = best[i]
        if c not in unique_colors:

    return best

def color_graph(adj: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
    n = len(adj)
    if n == 0:
        return []
    if n == 1:

        is_matrix = True
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(n):
                if adj[i][j] not in (0, 1):

                    break

    adj_list = [[] for _ in range(n)]

    if is_matrix:
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(n):
                if adj[i][j] == 1:
                    adj_list[i].append(j)
                    bit_adj[i] |= (1 << j)

        for i in range(n):
            for j in adj[i]:
                if j < n:  # safety check
                    adj_list[i].append(j)
                    bit_adj[i] |= (1 << j)

    def greedy_color(order):
        color = [-1] * n
        for v in order:
            used = 0
            for u in adj_list[v]:
                if color[u] != -1:
                    used |= (1 << color[u])
            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            color[v] = c
        return color
    
    # Helper: count colors used
    def count_colors(coloring):
        if not coloring:
            return 0
        return max(coloring) + 1

        for u in range(n):
            for v in adj_list[u]:
                if u < v and coloring[u] == coloring[v]:

    def dsatur():

            v = -1

            max_deg = -1
            for u in uncolored:
                # count distinct colors in sat[u]
                s = sat[u].bit_count()
                if s > max_sat or (s == max_sat and (deg[u] > max_deg or (deg[u] == max_deg and random.random() < 0.5))):
                    max_sat = s
                    max_deg = deg[u]
                    v = u
            if v == -1:
                break  # should not happen
            # assign smallest available color
            used = sat[v]
            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            color[v] = c
            uncolored.remove(v)
            # update neighbors
            for u in adj_list[v]:
                if u in uncolored:
                    sat[u] |= (1 << c)
                    deg[u] -= 1
        return color
    
    # Strategy 2: RLF (Recursive Largest First)
    def rlf():
        color = [-1] * n
        uncolored = set(range(n))
        c = 0
        while uncolored:
            # build maximal independent set for color c
            # degree in uncolored subgraph
            deg = {}
            for u in uncolored:
                deg[u] = sum(1 for v in adj_list[u] if v in uncolored)
            # start with max degree vertex
            v = max(uncolored, key=lambda x: deg[x])
            independent_set = {v}
            # U: vertices not adjacent to any in independent_set
            U = {u for u in uncolored if u != v and all(w not in adj_list[u] for w in independent_set)}
            # W: vertices adjacent to at least one in independent_set
            W = {u for u in uncolored if u not in independent_set and u not in U}
            while U:
                # select u in U with max |N(u) ∩ W|

                max_w_neighbors = -1

                    w_neighbors = sum(1 for w in adj_list[u] if w in W)

                        max_w_neighbors = w_neighbors
                        min_deg_u = deg[u]
                        best_u = u
                u = best_u
                independent_set.add(u)
                U.remove(u)
                # move neighbors of u from U to W
                for w in adj_list[u]:
                    if w in U:
                        U.remove(w)
                        W.add(w)
            # assign color c to independent_set
            for v in independent_set:
                color[v] = c
                uncolored.remove(v)
            c += 1
        return color

            order.append(v)

            for u in adj_list[v]:

                    # move u from bucket deg[u] to deg[u]-1
                    buckets[deg[u]].remove(u)
                    deg[u] -= 1
                    buckets[deg[u]].append(u)

    # We try to reduce colors by eliminating the highest color class

    improved = True

                        if v in target_vertices:
                            target_vertices.remove(v)

                if best_coloring[v] == target_color:
                    for c in range(target_color):

                        # We'll build the Kempe chain component containing v for colors c and target_color

                            if v in target_vertices:

                       (sat_u == max_sat and deg_u == max_deg and random.random() < 0.5):
                        max_sat = sat_u
                        max_deg = deg_u
                        v = u
            if v == -1:
                break  # should not happen

            # find smallest available color (mex)
            used = neighbor_colors[v]
            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            coloring[v] = c

            # update saturation and neighbor colors for neighbors
            for u in adj_list[v]:
                if coloring[u] == -1:
                    # if this color is new in u's neighborhood, increase saturation
                    if not (neighbor_colors[u] & (1 << c)):
                        neighbor_colors[u] |= (1 << c)
                        saturation[u] += 1
        return compact_colors(coloring)

    # RLF: Recursive Largest First
    def rlf():
        coloring = [-1] * n
        color = 0
        # uncolored set as bit mask
        R = (1 << n) - 1

        while R:
            # build independent set S for this color
            S = 0  # bit mask of vertices in S
            W = 0  # bit mask of vertices adjacent to S (ineligible)
            # U = R \ (S ∪ W) : eligible vertices

            # choose vertex with max degree in R
            v = -1
            max_deg = -1
            temp = R
            while temp:
                u = (temp & -temp).bit_length() - 1
                temp &= temp - 1
                # degree in R: popcount(bit_adj[u] & R)
                deg_in_R = (bit_adj[u] & R).bit_count()
                if deg_in_R > max_deg:
                    max_deg = deg_in_R
                    v = u
            if v == -1:
                break
            S |= (1 << v)
            R &= ~(1 << v)
            W |= (bit_adj[v] & R)  # neighbors of v in R become ineligible

            # expand S
            while True:
                # U = R & ~W
                U = R & ~W
                if U == 0:
                    break
                # select u in U with max |N(u) ∩ W|, tie-break by min degree in U
                u_best = -1
                max_nw = -1
                min_deg_u = float('inf')
                temp = U
                while temp:
                    u = (temp & -temp).bit_length() - 1
                    temp &= temp - 1
                    # |N(u) ∩ W|
                    nw = (bit_adj[u] & W).bit_count()
                    # degree in U
                    deg_in_U = (bit_adj[u] & U).bit_count()
                    if nw > max_nw or (nw == max_nw and deg_in_U < min_deg_u) or \
                       (nw == max_nw and deg_in_U == min_deg_u and random.random() < 0.5):
                        max_nw = nw
                        min_deg_u = deg_in_U
                        u_best = u
                if u_best == -1:
                    break
                # add u_best to S
                S |= (1 << u_best)
                R &= ~(1 << u_best)
                # move neighbors of u_best from U to W
                W |= (bit_adj[u_best] & R)  # R is updated, so neighbors still in R
            # assign color to all in S
            temp = S
            while temp:
                u = (temp & -temp).bit_length() - 1
                temp &= temp - 1
                coloring[u] = color
            color += 1
        return compact_colors(coloring)

    # Smallest-Last ordering (Matula & Beck)
    def smallest_last():
        # compute degeneracy ordering
        remaining = set(range(n))
        degree = [len(adj_list[i]) for i in range(n)]
        order = []
        # bucket sort by degree
        max_deg = max(degree) if n > 0 else 0
        buckets = [[] for _ in range(max_deg + 1)]
        for v in range(n):
            buckets[degree[v]].append(v)
        # pointer to current min degree
        min_deg = 0
        for _ in range(n):
            # find non-empty bucket
            while min_deg <= max_deg and not buckets[min_deg]:
                min_deg += 1
            if min_deg > max_deg:
                break
            v = buckets[min_deg].pop()
            order.append(v)
            # update neighbors
            for u in adj_list[v]:
                if u in remaining:
                    degree[u] -= 1
                    if degree[u] < len(buckets):
                        buckets[degree[u]].append(u)
            remaining.remove(v)
        # color in reverse order
        coloring = [-1] * n
        for v in reversed(order):
            used = 0
            for u in adj_list[v]:
                if coloring[u] != -1:
                    used |= (1 << coloring[u])
            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            coloring[v] = c
        return compact_colors(coloring)

    # Kempe chain color reduction
    def kempe_reduce(coloring):
        if not coloring:
            return coloring
        k = num_colors(coloring)
        # try to eliminate color classes from highest to lowest
        for target_color in range(k-1, 0, -1):
            # vertices with target_color
            vertices = [v for v in range(n) if coloring[v] == target_color]
            if not vertices:
                continue
            changed = True
            # iterate until no more changes or all vertices recolored
            while changed and vertices:
                changed = False
                v = vertices.pop()
                # try direct reassignment to a lower color
                for c in range(target_color):
                    conflict = False
                    for u in adj_list[v]:
                        if coloring[u] == c:
                            conflict = True
                            break
                    if not conflict:
                        coloring[v] = c
                        changed = True
                        break
                if changed:
                    continue
                # try Kempe chains with each lower color
                for c in range(target_color):
                    # BFS to find Kempe chain (target_color, c) containing v
                    from collections import deque
                    visited = [False] * n
                    queue = deque([v])
                    visited[v] = True
                    component = []
                    while queue:
                        x = queue.popleft()
                        component.append(x)
                        for y in adj_list[x]:
                            if not visited[y] and (coloring[y] == target_color or coloring[y] == c):
                                visited[y] = True
                                queue.append(y)
                    # check if any neighbor of v in the component has color c? Actually, we need to see
                    # if swapping frees color c for v: i.e., no neighbor of v has color c after swap
                    # After swap, v would get color c. So we need that no neighbor of v has color c
                    # in the current coloring, except possibly those in the component that will swap to target_color.
                    # Actually, if we swap, neighbors in the component that were target_color become c,
                    # and those that were c become target_color.
                    # So for v to safely take color c, we need that no neighbor of v is currently color c
                    # and outside the component (because inside, they would become target_color after swap).
                    # But wait: if a neighbor is in the component and has color c, after swap it becomes target_color,
                    # so it's okay. The only problem is if a neighbor has color c and is NOT in the component.
                    # Because then it stays c, and v would become c -> conflict.
                    safe = True
                    for u in adj_list[v]:
                        if coloring[u] == c and not visited[u]:
                            safe = False
                            break
                    if safe:
                        # perform swap: target_color <-> c in component
                        for x in component:
                            if coloring[x] == target_color:
                                coloring[x] = c
                            else:  # must be c
                                coloring[x] = target_color
                        changed = True
                        break
            # if we couldn't recolor all vertices of target_color, break and keep this color
            if vertices:  # some vertices remain of target_color
                break
        # compact colors again
        return compact_colors(coloring)

    # Run all heuristics
    best_coloring = None
    best_k = float('inf')

    for func in [dsatur, rlf, smallest_last]:
        coloring = func()
        if not is_valid(coloring):
            # fallback: should not happen, but just in case
            continue
        k = num_colors(coloring)
        if k < best_k or (k == best_k and best_coloring is None):
            best_k = k
            best_coloring = coloring

    # Apply Kempe reduction to improve
    if best_coloring is not None:
        improved = kempe_reduce(best_coloring)
        if is_valid(improved):
            k_improved = num_colors(improved)
            if k_improved < best_k:
                best_coloring = improved
                best_k = k_improved

    # Final validation and compacting
    if best_coloring is None:
        # ultimate fallback: greedy Welsh-Powell with random order
        order = list(range(n))
        random.shuffle(order)
        coloring = [-1] * n
        for v in order:
            used = 0
            for u in adj_list[v]:
                if coloring[u] != -1:
                    used |= (1 << coloring[u])
            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            coloring[v] = c
        best_coloring = compact_colors(coloring)

    return best_coloring

                neighbors[i].add(j)
                bit_adj[i] |= (1 << j)

    def is_valid(coloring):
        for u in range(n):
            for v in neighbors[u]:

                    return False
        return True

    def num_colors(coloring):
        return max(coloring) + 1 if coloring else 0

    # Helper: convert to consecutive colors starting from 0
    def normalize(coloring):
        if not coloring:
            return coloring
        mapping = {}
        next_color = 0
        for c in coloring:
            if c not in mapping:
                mapping[c] = next_color
                next_color += 1
        return [mapping[c] for c in coloring]

    # DSATUR
    def dsatur():
        coloring = [-1] * n
        # saturation degree: number of distinct colors in neighbors
        saturation = [0] * n

        colored_masks = [0] * n

        vertices = list(range(n))

            best_sat = -1
            best_deg = -1

                        best_sat = sat
                        best_deg = deg

                    used |= (1 << coloring[u])

            v = max(uncolored, key=lambda x: len([y for y in neighbors[x] if y in uncolored]))
            S.add(v)

            W = set()

                    continue

                    W.add(u)
                else:
                    U.add(u)

            while U:
                # select u in U with max |N(u) ∩ W|
                best_u = -1
                best_score = -1
                best_degU = -1
                for u in U:
                    score = len([w for w in neighbors[u] if w in W])
                    degU = len([w for w in neighbors[u] if w in U])
                    if score > best_score or (score == best_score and degU < best_degU) or (score == best_score and degU == best_degU and u < best_u):
                        best_score = score
                        best_degU = degU
                        best_u = u
                u = best_u
                S.add(u)
                U.remove(u)
                # move neighbors of u from U to W
                for w in list(U):
                    if w in neighbors[u]:
                        U.remove(w)
                        W.add(w)

                coloring[v] = color

    def smallest_last():
        # compute degeneracy ordering
        remaining = set(range(n))
        degree = [len(neighbors[i]) for i in range(n)]
        order = []

        buckets = [set() for _ in range(max_deg + 1)]
        for v in range(n):
            buckets[degree[v]].add(v)

        for _ in range(n):
            # find first non-empty bucket
            d = 0
            while d <= max_deg and not buckets[d]:
                d += 1
            if d > max_deg:
                break
            v = buckets[d].pop()
            order.append(v)
            # update neighbors
            for u in neighbors[v]:
                if u in remaining:
                    # remove u from its current bucket
                    old_deg = degree[u]
                    buckets[old_deg].remove(u)
                    degree[u] -= 1
                    new_deg = degree[u]
                    if new_deg <= max_deg:
                        buckets[new_deg].add(u)
                    else:
                        # should not happen
                        pass
            remaining.remove(v)
        # color in reverse order
        coloring = [-1] * n
        for v in reversed(order):
            used = 0
            for u in neighbors[v]:
                if coloring[u] != -1:
                    used |= (1 << coloring[u])
            c = 0
            while used & (1 << c):
                c += 1
            coloring[v] = c

                v = target_vertices.pop()

                        used |= (1 << coloring[u])

                        changed = True

                    target_vertices = [v for v in range(n) if coloring[v] == target_color]
                    continue
                # try Kempe chains with each lower color
                for c in range(target_color):
                    # if v already has color c after potential direct move, skip
                    if coloring[v] == c:

                    # BFS/DFS to get component

                    # Actually, swapping is safe if no neighbor of v in the component has color c?

                    # We want to know if after swap, v can take color c without conflict.
                    # After swap, v will have color c. It conflicts if any neighbor has color c.
                    # But in the component, neighbors with color c will become target_color, so no conflict.
                    # However, neighbors outside the component that are color c remain color c -> conflict.
                    # So we need: no neighbor of v outside the component has color c.
                    safe = True
                    for u in neighbors[v]:
                        if coloring[u] == c and u not in component:
                            safe = False
                            break
                    if safe:
                        # perform swap: target_color <-> c in component
                        for node in component:
                            if coloring[node] == target_color:
                                coloring[node] = c
                            else:  # must be c
                                coloring[node] = target_color

                        # rebuild target_vertices
                        target_vertices = [v for v in range(n) if coloring[v] == target_color]

            # if we couldn't eliminate this color class, break and try next lower target? 
            # Actually, we continue to try to reduce the same color class until no more changes.
            # But if we couldn't change any vertex in this class, we move to next lower target color.
            # However, standard approach is to try to eliminate the smallest color class.
            # We are iterating from high to low, so we try to eliminate high color classes first.
            # If we can't eliminate a color class, we leave it and try lower ones? 
            # But eliminating a high color class is better for reducing total colors.
            # We break after trying to reduce one color class? 
            # Actually, we want to try to eliminate the highest color class possible.
            # If we succeed in eliminating it (i.e., no vertex has target_color anymore), we break and restart from new highest.
            # But we are doing iterative improvement: after each successful swap, we check again.
            # We break out of the color loop only if we managed to eliminate the color class? 
            # Let's restructure: we will attempt to eliminate the current highest color class until no more moves.
            # If after trying all vertices we still have the color class, we move to next lower target.
            # But we already have a while changed loop inside.
            # After processing a target color, if there are still vertices with that color, we cannot eliminate it further.
            # So we continue to next lower target color.
        # compact colors: ensure they are 0..k-1
        return normalize(coloring)

    # Generate candidates
    candidates = []
    start_time = time.time()
    # DSATUR
    t0 = time.time()
    c1 = dsatur()
    t1 = time.time()
    if is_valid(c1):

    # RLF
    c2 = rlf()
    t2 = time.time()
    if is_valid(c2):
